hw_command.description: Clears VCRC01. Disables the ECE internal "flight test mode" intended for H/W testing in flight. See ECE board specs for details. Used in flight on an Isolated or stay-online ECE.
Clears VCRC02 Selects error correction for uplink to detect and report double errors and correct single bit errors. SECDED = single error correction, double error detection.
Clear VCRC03. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC04. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC05. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC06. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC07. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clear VCRC08. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clear VCRC09. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC10. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clear VCRC11. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC12. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clear VCRC13. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC14. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC15. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.

Clears VCRC16. Requests the system to enter Isolation mode on the next non-POR reset by clearing Go_Iso_Inv_state_crc16_pid32. Isolation mode is a state in which no FSW runs on this string, but the ECE is powered such that the other string may peek and poke at its memory.
Clears VCRC17. Directs SUROM to start with the FSW-selection NVCRCs.
Clears VCRC18. FSW will use the default non-volatile records when FSW initializes. FSW will additionally write the default values to non-volatile records and then set this CRC.
Clears VCRC19
Clears VCRC20. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC21 Lifts write protection of the write-protected contents on EMEM NAND.
Clears VCRC22. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC23. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears VCRC24. Lifts write protection of the FSW image in bank 0.
Clears VCRC25. Lifts write protection of the RAD750 V5 FPGA image in bank A as well as RTAX SUROM image A.
Clears VCRC26. Lifts write protection of the RAD750 V5 FPGA image in bank B as well as RTAX SUROM image B.
Clear VCRC27. Lifts write protection of the BDS FPGA V5 image on the BDS board.
Clears VCRC28. Lifts write protection of both JPL SUROM images in banks 0 and 1.
Clears VCRC29. Lifts write protection of both JPL SUROM images in banks 2 and 3.
Clears VCRC30. Lifts write protection of the FSW image in bank 1.
Clears VCRC31. Lifts write protection of the FSW image in bank 2.

Sets NVCRC32.
Toggling this CRC causes a wakeup signal to REU-A.
Connected to CRCC1.

Sets NVCRC33.
Toggling this CRC causes a wakeup signal to REU-B.
Connected to CRCC2.

Clears NVCRC34.
Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears NVCRC35. During Zombie initialization, FSW will use the retrieved records in NPM if NVCRC35 is clear.
Clears NVCRC36. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears NVCRC37. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears NVCRC38. Enables the FDU local watchdog.

Clears NVCRC39. Disables the fault response to a detected Virtex 5 configuration RAM upset on the RAD750. This means the ECE will not be reset, the Virtex 5 will not be reprogrammed, and FSW can continue to operate. Note that it is possible the Virtex 5 will behave incorrectly / unpredictably which could result in the ECE resetting anyway.
Clears NVCRC40. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.

Clears NVCRC41.
Used in conjunction with SSE commands to enable test mode or force flight mode. Flight mode will ensure FSW uses the system mode history during FSW prime initialization.

Sets NVCRC42. Need two cmds to select a SUROM bank: Need two cmds to select a SUROM bank: To select SUROM bank 3, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_1 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_1. To select SUROM bank 2, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_1 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_0. To select SUROM bank 1, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_0 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_1. To select SUROM bank 0, HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_0 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_0.
Sets NVCRC43. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC. Connected to CRCC4.

Sets NVCRC44. Configures the RAD750 FPGA such that on the next POR, the FPGA will be loaded with the image from bank B. Connected to CRCC5 and drives the state of PID41.
This command issues a clear, but H/W will "set" relay CRCC5. The state of NVCRC44 will be "1". The connected PID41 inverts the input to show "0", and on the next POR, it will use V5 bank B/1/MRAM2 = 0xbee0_0000 (RTAX SUROM).

Sets NVCRC45. Need two cmds to select a SUROM bank: Need two cmds to select a SUROM bank: To select SUROM bank 3, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_1 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_1. To select SUROM bank 2, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_1 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_0. To select SUROM bank 1, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_0 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_1. To select SUROM bank 0, HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_0 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_0.

Sets CRC46. Each REU XORs the input from the ECE relay to hold the REU in reset or not. If ECE-A NVCRC-46 and ECE-B NVCRC-46 are both "1" or both "0", REU-A is not inhibited. If either ECE's CRC is "1" and the other "0", REU-A will be inhibited.
Clears NVCRC47. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.

Clears NVCRC48, but the PIDs used by SUROM invert the input so this command is the logical selection "1". Need two cmds to select a FSW image bank: Select FSW image bank 0, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL0 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL0. Select FSW image bank 1, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL0 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL1. Select FSW image bank 2, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL1 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL0. Select FSW image bank 3: , HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL1 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL1.

Clears NVCRC49, but the PIDs used by SUROM invert the input so this command is the logical selection "1". Need two cmds to select a FSW image bank: Select FSW image bank 0, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL0 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL0. Select FSW image bank 1, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL0 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL1. Select FSW image bank 2, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL1 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL0. Select FSW image bank 3: , HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL1 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL1.

Clears NVCRC50. Clears the request to enter Zombie mode on the next reset. Zombie mode is a reduced-capability mode that will get the vehicle safe and complete critical events, but this String cannot do science.
Clears NVCRC51. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears NVCRC52. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears NVCRC53. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears NVCRC54. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.

Sets CRC55. Each REU XORs the input from the ECE relay to hold the REU in reset or not.
If ECE-A NVCRC-55 and ECE-B NVCRC-55 are both "1" or both "0", REU-B is not inhibited. If either ECE's CRC is "1" and the other "0", REU-B will be inhibited.
Clears NVCRC56. Spare CRC/PID.
Clears NVCRC57. Un-inhibits EDAC on the EIO board.
Clears NVCRC58. Un-inhibits EDAC on the EMEM board.
Clears NVCRC59. Un-inhibits EDAC on the BDS boards.

Clears NVCRC60. Disables the system to from entering Zombie mode on subsequent resets. Zombie mode is a reduced-capability mode that will get the vehicle safe and complete critical events, but this String cannot do science.
Clears NVCRC61. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Clears NVCRC62.
Clears NVCRC63. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.

Sets VCRC00. Forces ECE to reset (but does not reset the BDS, payload interfaces, or IMU interfaces).
Sets VCRC01. Enables the ECE internal flight-test mode intended for H/W testing in-flight. See ECE board specs for details. Used in flight on an Isolated or stay-online ECE.
Sets VCRC02 Selects error correction for uplink to detect triple errors but won't correct single bit errors. NECTED = no error correction, triple error detection.
Sets VCRC03. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC04. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC05. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC06. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC07. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC08. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC09. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC10. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC11. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC12. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC13. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC14. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC15. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.

Sets VCRC16. Requests the system to clear Isolation mode request on the next reset by setting Go_Iso_Inv_state_crc16_pid32. Isolation mode is a state in which no FSW runs on this string, but the ECE is powered such that the other string may peek and poke at its memory.
Sets VCRC17. Directs SUROM to use the internal logic to select the FSW bank
Sets VCRC18. FSW will use the retrieved non-volatile records when FSW initializes. This is the POR state of the CRC.
Sets VCRC19
Sets VCRC20. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC22. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC23. Spare volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets VCRC24. Enables write protection of the FSW image in bank 0.
Sets VCRC25. Enables write protection of the RAD750 V5 FPGA image in bank A as well as RTAX SUROM image A.
Sets VCRC26. Enables write protection of the RAD750 V5 FPGA image in bank B as well as RTAX SUROM image B.
Sets VCRC27. Enables write protection of the BDS FPGA V5 image on the BDS board.
Sets VCRC28. Enables write protection of both JPL SUROM images in banks 0 and 1.
Sets VCRC29. Enables write protection of both JPL SUROM images in banks 2 and 3.
Sets VCRC30. Enables write protection of the FSW image in bank 1.
Sets VCRC31. Enables write protection of the FSW image in bank 2.

Clears NVCRC32.
Toggling this CRC causes a wakeup signal to REU-A.
Connected to CRCC1.

Clears NVCRC33.
Toggling this CRC causes a wakeup signal to REU-B.
Connected to CRCC2.

Sets NVCRC34.
Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets NVCRC35. During Zombie initialization, FSW will use the default non-volatile records if NVCRC35 is set.
Sets NVCRC36. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets NVCRC37. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets NVCRC38. Neuters the FDU such that H/W toggles the healthbeat discretes without FSW having to meet all the local watchdog checks.
Sets NVCRC39. This has the effect of enabling the fault response to a detected Virtex 5 configuration RAM upset in the RAD750. The response is to reset the ECE and re-program the Virtex 5 FPGA.
Sets NVCRC40. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.

Sets NVCRC41.
Used in conjunction with SSE commands to inform FSW (during prime initialization) to enter SYS_TEST mode or to use the last saved system mode from REU shared records.

Clears NVCRC42. Need two cmds to select a SUROM bank: To select SUROM bank 3, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_1 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_1. To select SUROM bank 2, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_1 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_0. To select SUROM bank 1, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_0 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_1. To select SUROM bank 0, HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_0 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_0.
Clears NVCRC43. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC. Connected to CRCC4.

Clears NVCRC44. Configures the RAD750 FPGA such that on the next POR, the FPGA will be loaded with the image from bank A. Connected to CRCC5 and drives the state of PID41.
This command issues a set, but H/W will "clear" relay CRCC5. The state of NVCRC44 will be "0". The connected PID41 inverts the input to show "1", and on the next POR, it will use V5 bank A/0/MRAM1 = 0xbe60_0000 (RTAX SUROM).

Clears NVCRC45. Need two cmds to select a SUROM bank: Need two cmds to select a SUROM bank: To select SUROM bank 3, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_1 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_1. To select SUROM bank 2, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_1 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_0. To select SUROM bank 1, send HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_0 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_1. To select SUROM bank 0, HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC45_LOGICAL_0 & HDW_SELECT_SUROM_CRC42_LOGICAL_0.

Clears CRC46. Each REU XORs the input from the ECE relay to hold the REU in reset or not. If ECE-A NVCRC-46 and ECE-B NVCRC-46 are both "1" or both "0", REU-A is not inhibited. If either ECE's CRC is "1" and the other "0", REU-A will be inhibited.
Sets NVCRC47. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.

Sets NVCRC48, but the PIDs used by SUROM invert the input so this command is the logical selection "0". Need two cmds to select a FSW image bank:
Select FSW image bank 0, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL0 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL0.
Select FSW image bank 1, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL0 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL1.
Select FSW image bank 2, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL1 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL0.
Select FSW image bank 3: , HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL1 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL1.

Sets NVCRC49, but the PIDs used by SUROM invert the input so this command is the logical selection "0". Need two cmds to select a FSW image bank: Select FSW image bank 0, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL0 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL0. Select FSW image bank 1, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL0 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL1. Select FSW image bank 2, HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL1 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL0. Select FSW image bank 3: , HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC49_LOGICAL1 & HDW_SELECT_FSW_IMG_CRC48_LOGICAL1.

Sets NVCRC50. Requests the system to enter Zombie mode on the next reset IF Zombie mode has been enabled (via the H/W command HDW_ENABLE_ZOMBIE_MODE. Zombie mode is a reduced-capability mode that will get the vehicle safe and complete critical events, but this String cannot do science.
Sets NVCRC51. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets NVCRC52. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets NVCRC53. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets NVCRC54. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.

Clears CRC55. Each REU XORs the input from the ECE relay to hold the REU in reset or not. If ECE-A NVCRC-55 and ECE-B NVCRC-55 are both "1" or both "0", REU-B is not inhibited. If either ECE's CRC is "1" and the other "0", REU-B will be inhibited.
Sets NVCRC56. Spare CRC/PID.
Sets NVCRC57. Inhibits EDAC on the EIO board.
Sets NVCRC58. Inhibits EDAC on the EMEM board.
Sets NVCRC59 Inhibits EDAC on the BDS boards.

Sets NVCRC60. Enables the system to enter Zombie mode on the next reset. FSW will only enter Zombie mode if this CRC is SET and either FSW or Operators have additionally requested to "go Zombie". The additional ground command is HDW_GO_ZOMBIE. Zombie mode is a reduced-capability mode that will get the vehicle safe and complete critical events, but this String cannot do science.
Sets NVCRC61. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.
Sets NVCRC62.
Sets NVCRC63. Spare non-volatile HCD/CRC.

unsigned_arg.name: trigger_time
unsigned_arg.description: Time trigger of when to change to the new SCLK time. If set to 0 it will take effect immediately.

fsw_command.description: Command to set the Spacecraft clock to the specified SCLK seconds. If the trigger time is in the past (with respect to receipt of command) the command is executed immediately. FSW will cancel a previous time command if a new one comes in before the time change occurs. The command provides 1-2 seconds of SCLK controllability for when the SCLK change is immediate (because it's possible to receive the command right after sending STM, meaning the new commanded SCLK value will not take effect until the next full second boundary). An EVR will report command received and waiting for time to apply new time change (EHA will not reflect the new time at this time). When trigger time expires an EVR will report the new time change. Once the command is processed, all executing sequences are deactivated. See Timekeeping FDD D-56168 for more information.
fsw_command.completion: Completes when SCLK seconds value is either updated or the command is cancelled by a subsequent command.

mode.reason: S/C attached to LV. Priming can not take place until after seperation.

unsigned_arg.name: dp_priority
unsigned_arg.description: This argument controls the data product priority of the data products produced as a result of this command. A priority of 0 will result in the default data product priority being used.

unsigned_arg.name: duration
unsigned_arg.description: Duration to collect the propulsion pressure data product.

fsw_command.description:
This command initiates the collection of the propulsion pressure data product which contains high rates of various pressures. If commanded when another collection is in progress, the new commanded duration will be the remaining duration. A duration of 0 will terminate an in progress dump.
If a DP is being collected with a certain priority and a new command is issued with a different priority. The old priority DP will be closed, and the new priority DP will be opened and will continue on with collecting based on the modified collection time behavior.
fsw_command.completion: This command completes when the data product collection duration has been set.

enum_arg.name: prop_which_pt
enum_arg.description: The prop pressure transducer pair to turn on/off. The command is able to turn on/off all 16 propulsion PT's at once using this enum. ON commands will be rejected if any of the PTs in the PT pair argument are SICK or DEAD. OFF commands will be sent if any of if any of the PTs in the PT pair argument are SICK or DEAD. If the argument is "all" to power on all 16 PT's, then the healthy PT pairs will still be powered on, while the unhealthy PT's are not.

enum_arg.name: prop_desired_pt_state
enum_arg.description: The target state of the specified pressure transducer pair (on or off)

fsw_command.description: A command to power on or power off specified pressure transducer pair. The commanding is done via the prime PM side PME.

enum_arg.name: bds_system_configuration
enum_arg.description: Desired BDS configuration

fsw_command.description:
Configure the BDS to one of three operational modes:
UART_HS_ONLY: BDS NAND, BDSM, DDR2, and BDS V5 are all powered off. LRC is on. No instrument recording to BDS. UART instrument H&S is available but no SpW instrument H&S. UART instruments are command-able, but no SpW instrument commanding.
NO_SPW_RECORDING: LRC, BDS NAND, BDSM, DDR2, and BDS V5 are all powered on, but no SpW instrument data is recorded to BDS. UART recording is still available. H&S for all instruments is available. All instruments are command-able.
FULL_OPERATIONAL: LRC, BDS NAND, BDSM, DDR2, and BDS V5 are all powered on. All instrument data is recorded, H&S for all instruments is available and all instruments are command-able.
Note that if any of the following behaviors is in progress, the transition to UART_HS_ONLY will be rejected. You must issue the DDM_STOP_BDS_ACTION command first. - Any cross-string BDS behavior - Any filter - Radiation maintenance - Any format - Dump unfiltered recording Additionally, stop any XS BDS behavior before commanding the Online ECE's BDS to UART_HS_ONLY mode.
fsw_command.completion: After desired configuration has been achieved (or quit).

fsw_command.description: This command checks the file size and if the file size is smaller than the allotted size, FSW installs the contents into the specified area. Then FSW will validate the image in place, comparing the calculated and expected checksum. An EVR will be issued with the computed checksum, expected checksum, and version (from the header). The command fails if the checksum comparison fails either on reading the original file or after it has been loaded into BDS MRAM.

fsw_command.description:
Command to request a data dump of the ACS_CTL input and output structures associated with data generated from the algorithms and Device Managers. This will collect 32 Hz and 8 Hz MDPs and CDPs. fsw_command.description: Copies the contents of a file to the selected REU. Big Endian. File size limit = 40960 words (81920 bytes). Depending on starting address, the command will disable the related write protection before writing memory and enable the related write protection after. User of this command should not cross write protect/memory regions. Reject command if REU is currently in power on or resync behavior, if another REU_COPY_FILE is currently in progress, or if the end address (calculated from starting address and file size) is greater than the end of a WP boundary. Also reject command if REU expected state is off, or if REU_DMP_MEMORY is currently in progress.
fsw_command.completion: The file is written to REU memory.

enum_arg.name: which_format_type
enum_arg.description: What type of format: Logical: Erases only the 'used' area of the array, resetting all Logical statistics and rebuilding the blank file catalog. This includes all 'Allocated' Stripes which were pending operation but some non-graceful termination of ECE behavior left them marked in MRAM. Physical: Re-Erases the entire array including all previously erased content but keeps the accumulated bad block and wear-leveling statistics. NOTE: Will attempt re-erasure of any suspect stripes. Factory_restore: Restores the memory to the factory delivered state and clears all the wear-leveling and sets the bad block statistics to the factory detected values. This format type is idempotent resulting in the same MRAM and NAND state regardless of the pre-condition (baring failed operations during the action).

fsw_command.description: Formats BDS NAND and updates the MRAM catalog and stats. Will skip suspect stripes on a logical or physical format, but factory restore does not. This command will be rejected if not in the NO_SPW_RECORDING BDS operational state. Additionally, this command will be rejected if recording has not been stopped (via the AVS_ACTIVATE_BDS_RECORDING command) or if a filter, radiation maintenance, or x-string copy activity is in progress.
fsw_command.completion: When formatting completes.

enum_arg.name: RAM_ADDRESS_TYPE
enum_arg.description: Type of addressing

unsigned_arg.name: start_addr
unsigned_arg.description: Starting address must be word aligned (2 LSBs are 0) and non-zero.

unsigned_arg.name: end_addr
unsigned_arg.description: Ending/last address to read. Length of request (end_addr - start_addr + 1) must be word align, thus the end_addr 2 LSBs should be 1s.

enum_arg.name: make_dp
enum_arg.description: make_dp

unsigned_arg.name: dp_priority
unsigned_arg.description: DP priority if a DP is made

fsw_command.description:
FSW reads out contents of contiguous SRAM, DDR2 or MRAM, computes the CRC32, and writes contents to a DP if make_dp is "yes". The CRC result plus any errors indicated by H/W and the error address is reported in the corresponding EVR(s).
The start address must be word aligned (2 LSBs are 0), and the total length of the read must be word aligned as well.
FSW will reject the command if the start and end addresses are not contiguously mapped. FSW will reject the command if the start address is not word aligned. FSW will reject the command if the length of the request is not word aligned.
Note that the maximum size for a data product is 48 MiB.
Note that there is a SFC MRAM read idiosyncrasy in which the specified address needs to be adjusted based on the SUROM bank selection CRCs. This is documented in D-56146 ECE FDD (Appendix B).
fsw_command.completion: After the checksum EVR is issued

unsigned_arg.name: which_block
unsigned_arg.description: Which block

enum_arg.name: bb_state
enum_arg.description: Which state

fsw_command.description:
Marks an EMEM NAND block either good or bad. If operators mark a block "good", FSW will make it good only if the factory setting is not bad. In other words, this command won't undo the factory setting.
FSW will update the bad block code of the specified block and update the volume metadata if the block is present in a mounted volume. Else the volume metadata will be updated after mounting.
When marking a block bad the volume mount status doesn't matter.
When marking a block good, the command will be rejected if the volume is not mounted.
When marking a block good this command updates the wear count to be equal to the maximum wear of any block in the volume which the stripe belongs.
fsw_command.completion: When the block has been updated.

fsw_command.description:
Marks an EMEM NAND stripe either good or bad. FSW will update the bad block code of all blocks which compose the stripe and update the volume metadata if the stripe is present in a mounted volume. Else the volume metadata will be updated after mounting.
When marking a stripe bad the volume mount status doesn't matter.
When marking a stripe good, the command will be rejected if the volume is not mounted.
When marking a stripe good this command updates the stripe wear count to be equal to the maximum wear of any stripe in the volume which the stripe belongs. This updates the wear counts for all blocks which compose the stripe.
fsw_command.completion: When the stripe has been updated

enum_arg.name: which_pumps
enum_arg.description: Select which pump or group of pumps to turn ON or OFF.

enum_arg.name: pumps_mode
enum_arg.description: Specifies whether to turn selected pump or pump group ON or OFF.

enum_arg.name: other_pumps_mode
enum_arg.description: Specifies what to do with the rest of the HRS pumps (OFF or NO_TOUCH). When commanding a pump OFF, the other pumps will always be left NO_TOUCH (the other_pumps_mode argument will be ignored).

fsw_command.description:
Configures the power states of the 6 HRS pumps. Pumps can be commanded individually or in pre-defined groups (including PRIMES).
When both pumps on a side are commanded ON (either the "_BOTH" or "ALL" options), the downstream pump (designated "2") is turned on first, followed by the upstream pump ("1"), after a parameterized delay.
When both pumps on side are commanded OFF (either directly or through the other_pumps_mode argument), the upstream pump is powered OFF, followed by the delay, then the downstream pump.
Things to note: - This command will fail if which_pumps = ALL, pumps_mode = OFF, and the system mode is not SYS_TEST (do not turn ALL pumps off in flight) - For any value of which_pumps, if pumps_mode = OFF, FSW will not touch the other pumps (effectively ignoring the other_pumps_mode argument in this scenario) - FSW will not prevent operators from turning all pumps off by directly commanding each pump OFF. It will only reject the case where which_pumps is ALL and pumps_mode is OFF. - The delay parameter is THRM_PUMP_PWR_DELAY
fsw_command.completion: behavior is complete

This command needs to check against the discrete command shown in telemetry and confirm it matches what FSW expects. After sending this command, FSW will wait the appropriate number of RTIs and then check if the discrete command shown in telemetry matches what FSW expects. If the discrete telemetry check does not match, the command needs to be retried once and a retry EVR needs to be sent. If the redundant side PSS is not marked healthy, this command should be rejected (e.g. if PSS-1B is not healthy, reject this command for PSS-1A). fsw_command.description: The curve tracer function operates by biasing a test solar cell with current and simultaneously measuring the voltage across the cell. unsigned_arg.name: pwr_kp_setpoint
unsigned_arg.description: Kp: Proportional factor for current loop. The proportional factor Kp is a multiplier which reacts at the output and tries to adjust the gap between the output level and the setpoint at the input. However, an offset between input and output may remain.

unsigned_arg.name: pwr_ki_setpoint
unsigned_arg.description: Ki: Integral factor for current loop.The Integral section integrates the error signal and defines the speed that the controller should react to the errors. The bigger the error, the faster the response time. This section is weighted with an integral factor of Ki.

unsigned_arg.name: pwr_kd_setpoint
unsigned_arg.description: Kd: Derivative factor for current loop. The derivative section defines the ramp rate or slope at the output. It helps also to overcome the offset left from the proportional factor Kp. In addition, it ensures that the output does not overshoot over the setpoint (or stays within the limit) and prevents it from oscillation that may have been caused by integrator. This section is weighted with a derivative factor of Kd.

fsw_command.description:
This command will set the kp, ki and kd setpoints for the PID controller. Refer to the PBC IICD D-56604 and IPBC FPGA D-56651 (Section 3.7.3) for more information.
A PID controller consists of three elements: Proportional, Integral, Derivative
fsw_command.completion: Check if command completion EVR was sent.

fsw_command.description:

Command to request the collection of DP_GNC_DVE_ONTIME_OUTPUT data product. This DP collects 8Hz accumulated thruster on-times and 32Hz delta-V estimates. If commanded when another collection is in progress, the new commanded duration will be the remaining duration. A duration of 0 will terminate an in progress dump.

enum_arg.description: which NAND group

unsigned_arg.name: what_configuration
unsigned_arg.description: See EMEM spec, registers EMEMN_NAND_GR_A/B_LANE_SEL_T for details

fsw_command.description:
Sets the desired selection of the physical NAND devices/lanes used for data, ECC, and the spare. This command sets the desired state in the non-volatile file system metadata, for FSW to use when cloning, erasing, or during FSW initialization at the mount NAND step. At those times, FSW will then set the register in the EMEM board to this value. In other words, there is no change is made to the NAND configuration when this command is executed, but the value is used in subsequent events.
See the EMEM spec, registers EMEMN_NAND_GR_A_LANE_SEL_T and EMEMN_NAND_GR_B_LANE_SEL_T. Note that bits 31:23 are ignored in the command.
fsw_command.completion: Once FSW updates the desired state in MRAM.

unsigned_arg.name: what_configuration
unsigned_arg.description: See the High Rate Control (HRC) FPGA Specification for the configurations in the "BDSM group select register".

fsw_command.description:
Sets the desired selection of four NAND groups including which stacks are spares. The command sets the desired state in non-volatile BDS stripe metadata. FSW uses this value to configure the BDSM when it commands the BDS NAND on. In other words, there is no change is made to the NAND configuration when this command is executed, but the value is used in subsequent events.
Then FSW rebuilds the stripe map and saves to metadata.
FSW will reject this command if the BDS mode is not UART_HS_ONLY mode.
See the High Rate Control (HRC) FPGA Specification for the configurations in the "BDSM group select register".
fsw_command.completion: Once FSW updates the desired state in MRAM.

fsw_command.description:
This command will Isolate the backup REU by simultaneously inducing a self-check fail in it and marking it SICK. Note: if FSW is unable to verify the self-check fail then it will power off the REU. This command is necessary when the ground wants to operationally isolate a REU to prevent it from being in an intermediate state where it is SICK but not self-checked or self-checked but not SICK.
This command will also battle short the prime REU which disables its self-check mechanism and OVP.
This command will be rejected if the backup REU is OFF.
The SFP_COMMAND_BEHAVIOR_TIMEOUT parameter value is used for this command - if exceeded FSW will FATAL.

fsw_command.description: This command will send a discrete output command to inhibit or un-inhibit the selected PBC FPGA. Refer to D-56606 PCDA IICD for more details. This command needs to check against the discrete command shown in telemetry and confirm it matches what FSW expects. After sending this command, FSW will wait the appropriate number of RTIs and then check if the discrete command shown in telemetry matches what FSW expects. If the discrete telemetry check does not match, the command needs to be retried once and a retry EVR needs to be sent. When an un-inhibit command is sent, report the state of their POR and Soft-reset bits in an EVR (bits 15 and 14 respectively of TLM_01).

enum_arg.name: cmd_type_on_sru_mram
enum_arg.description: Command Type on the MRAM [0=Asleep (Lock), 1=No Sleep (Unlock)]

enum_arg.name: sru_mram_scanning_flag
enum_arg.description: MRAM scanning Flag (0=No scanning, 1= Scanning)

fsw_command.description: The Asleep/No sleep status of MRAM memory is reported in the Status tlm SecondStatus field (bit 2: 0 = Asleep / 1 = No Sleep). Memory Read/Write TC commands (sections 7.13 and 7.14 of SRU vendor ICD) that are addressing MRAM ranges will be accepted ONLY if the corresponding MRAM is unlocked (No sleep status). If the MRAM is locked (Asleep status), the write or read command is invalid (bit 1 in the SecondStatus field of the Status TM). By default, at the power ON (cold reset), the MRAM memory is in the Deep Sleep operation [RD6] after the loading of software code from MRAM to RAM memory. After a warm reset, the MRAM is automatically unlocked in order to access to MRAM (exit the Deep Sleep operation) and to upload the code from MRAM to RAM. After this loading the MRAM is automatically locked in order to enter Deep Sleep operation and the scanning of MRAM is disabled. This Asleep/No Sleep command allows also checking the integrity of MRAM memory by scanning the memory on request. This scanning status of MRAM is reported in the SecondStatus field (Bit 3: 0=No scanning/ 1= Scanning). The errors are recorded in Diagnostics telemetry during this scanning (EDAC errors). This command is rejected if the scanning is requested while the MRAM is locked. After this checking, Sodern recommends to lock MRAM in order to enter deep sleep operation for radiation requirement.
fsw_command.completion: After the command has been sent.

unsigned_arg.name: expected_checksum
unsigned_arg.description: Expected checksum of source file.

fsw_command.description: FSW fails this cmd if the which_bank argument is the currently HW CRC selected bank. FSW retrieves the filesystem checksum from the specified file and compares it to the expected checksum (supplied in the command). If the checksums do not match or if the file size is larger than the allotted space, the command fails. If the checksums match and the file size is under the max image size, FSW lifts write protection for this bank, copies the contents of the file to the specified SFC RTAX SUROM bank, then restores write protects. This command will fail if the write protection CRC is masked.
fsw_command.completion: When the write protects have been restored

unsigned_arg.name: raw_frames
unsigned_arg.description: Total run-time of image acquisition (in terms of FPE image frames). Any value from 0 to 1,048,575 may be set. A value of 0 enables continuous acquisition until aborted. Ideally, the value written would be the calculated number of frames received from the FPE necessary to generate the exact number of fully processed output frames. enum_arg.name: AVS_BDS_NAND_POWER_TYPE
enum_arg.description: ON - will power on all active stacks OFF - will gracefully power off all stacks, including spares (in a manner that does not lose already buffered data) CYCLE - will combine OFF and ON with a 2 second delay in between ON_ALL - will power on all stacks

fsw_command.description:
Command that can control the power to the NAND stacks on the BDSM. Even though the EM/FM hardware supports individually toggling NAND power, this will always power OFF all stacks, but on EM/FM only power ON active stacks (not the 4 spare stacks).
For OFF, handle it gracefully such that the already buffered data is recorded.
For the CYCLE argument, the power must remain off for at least 1 second, and without interrupting the recording of all UART instrument data. (i.e., disable recording, let it buffer up in DDR-2 while the NAND is power cycled, then resume recording)
Command should continue on errors (e.g. if detected power state does not match expected)
Command should leave NAND recording in the same state it was in at the beginning
Command should generate WARNING EVRs if the detected NAND power state does not match the commanded state.
Command should generate an ACTIVITY LO EVR any time the power state is modified.
If in the middle of a BDS mode change, reject this command. If in the middle of this command, queue a BDS mode change. If in UART_HS_ONLY or UNKNOWN, reject this command. If in the middle of a BDS activity/behavior - filter, radmaint, xstring copy, format - reject this command. If recording to NAND is active, accept and execute this command.
fsw_command.completion: The command is complete after power is restored and recording to NAND is resumed.

fsw_command.description:
This command power cycles the EMEM NAND (both banks) in a non-disruptive manner to ongoing file system accesses. NAND must remain off for at least 1 second.
Continue on errors (e.g. if power state does not match expected)
Generate WARNING EVR is the detected power state does not match the commanded state.
Generate ACTIVITY LO EVR any time the NAND power state is modified.
fsw_command.completion: Command completes after power is restored and file system access is resumed.

enum_arg.name: which_sru_eu
enum_arg.description: The SRU Electronics Unit the command is intended for.

fsw_command.description:
Command to update the SRU hardware's Julian date with SCLK + 315619200 seconds.
The HW expects Julian date to be seconds from 12am (midnight) Jan 1, 2000. Clipper SCLK starts at 12am Jan 1, 2010. SRU Julian Date is in seconds (uint32) SCLK (seconds) 315,619,200 (number of seconds between 12am Jan 1, 2000 and 12am Jan1, 2010). A flight rule will dictate the minimum frequency between SRU Julian date updates.
fsw_command.completion: Once the command has been sent.
